los.text: Perform a structured clinical examination of the knee.
los.html:
StepDetail
Look (standing)Gait, varus/valgus deformity, quadriceps wasting, swelling, popliteal (Baker's) cyst
Look (lying)Scars, redness, swelling, fixed flexion
FeelTemperature, effusion: patellar tap (large) or sweep/bulge test (small); joint line tenderness (knee flexed: meniscal), patella, tibial tuberosity, popliteal fossa
MoveActive and passive flexion (~135°) and extension (0°), crepitus; straight leg raise (extensor mechanism)
Special testsAnterior/posterior drawer and Lachman's (cruciates), valgus/varus stress at 20–30° flexion (MCL/LCL), McMurray's (meniscus), patellar apprehension
  • Finish: examine the hip (referred pain) and neurovascular status; X-ray (weight-bearing).

los.text: Perform a clinical examination of the shoulder with increasing confidence and accuracy
los.html:
• Full routine: see ICM Year 1 › Musculoskeletal › LO 1 (look, feel, move, special tests).
Accuracy tips
Watch from behind during abduction: scapulohumeral rhythm, painful arc
Compare passive external rotation with the other side (frozen shoulder)
Name the rotator cuff muscle each test isolates
Check the neck as a source of pain

los.text: Demonstrate the ability to perform a gastrointestinal examination with clinical competence, interpret and integrate findings with relevant knowledge to support clinical reasoning, and clearly present these findings to peers or supervisors.
los.html:
• Full routine: see ICM Year 1 › Gastrointestinal & liver › LO 1.
Competence =
Fluent, complete sequence including finishing steps (hernias, genitalia, DRE, urine dip)
Interpret: chronic liver disease stigmata, organomegaly, ascites, masses, peritonism
Integrate with the history and present: positives, negatives, summary, differential, investigations (bloods incl. LFTs, ultrasound, CT)

los.text: Demonstrate a systematic musculoskeletal examination of the hand and wrist, accurately identifying anatomical landmarks, assessing function, and recognizing abnormal findings
los.html:
StepDetail
LookDorsum and palm: swelling, deformity, wasting, scars, skin and nails
FeelTemperature, MCP squeeze, palpate each joint, anatomical snuffbox, radial styloid, distal radioulnar joint, ulnar styloid
MoveWrist flexion (80°)/extension (70°), radial/ulnar deviation, pronation/supination; fingers and thumb
FunctionGrip, pinch, button, write
NervesMedian, ulnar, radial (motor and sensory)
Special testsPhalen's, Tinel's, Finkelstein's, scaphoid compression
Abnormal findingSuggests
Snuffbox tendernessScaphoid fracture
Pain on Finkelstein'sDe Quervain's tenosynovitis
Dorsal "dinner fork" deformityColles' fracture
Smooth lump on dorsumGanglion (transilluminates)
Triggering fingerStenosing tenosynovitis (A1 pulley)
